examples.text:

glosses: An impression of such stamp on wax, paper or other material used for sealing.

examples.text: The front of the podium bore the presidential seal.

So the matter rested until the Cranbrook & Paddock Wood Company was incorporated on August 8, 1877, appropriately displaying a bunch of hops on its seal, for these had become the principal cash crop in the area.

glosses: Anything that secures or authenticates.
Something which will be visibly damaged if a covering or container is opened, and which may or may not bear an official design.

examples.text: The result was declared invalid, as the seal on the meter had been broken.
Seals were placed on the papal apartment on the third floor of the Apostolic Palace and on the apartment on the second floor of the Casa Santa Marta, where Pope Francis lived.

glosses: Confirmation or approval, or an indication of this.

examples.text: Her clothes always had her mom's seal of approval.

glosses: Something designed to prevent liquids or gases from leaking through a joint.

examples.text: The canister is leaking. I think the main seal needs to be replaced.

glosses: A tight closure, secure against leakage.

examples.text: Close the lid tightly to get a good seal.

glosses: A chakra.
To place a seal on (a document).
To mark with a stamp, as an evidence of standard exactness, legal size, or merchantable quality.

examples.text: to seal weights and measures
to seal silverware

glosses: To fasten (something) so that it cannot be opened without visible damage.

examples.text: The cover is sealed. If anyone tries to open it, we'll know about it.

glosses: To prevent people or vehicles from crossing (something).

examples.text: The border has been sealed until the fugitives are found.

glosses: To close securely to prevent leakage.

examples.text: I've sealed the bottle to keep the contents fresh.
Seal up your lips, and give no words but "mum".

glosses: To place in a sealed container.

examples.text: I've sealed the documents in this envelope.

glosses: To place a notation of one's next move in a sealed envelope to be opened after an adjournment.

examples.text: After thinking for half an hour, the champion sealed his move.

glosses: To guarantee.

examples.text: The last-minute goal sealed United’s win.
seal one's destiny
seal someone's fate
seal the job
England's first-half display contained much to admire but it was a sign of their wastefulness in front of goal that it took the injury-time intervention from Kane to seal victory.

glosses: To fix, as a piece of iron in a wall, with cement or plaster, etc.

examples.text: Sealed to this wall by their rims were cazuelas ( earthenware bowls).

glosses: To close by means of a seal.

examples.text: to seal a drainpipe with water
When the silicone rubber has set the plaster pieces are replaced, followed by the lid, which is sealed to the mother-mould with plaster and bandage as previously described.

glosses: To bind eternally as family members.

examples.text: If a man once married desires a second helpmate […] she is sealed to him under the solemn sanction of the church.
She can be sealed to this other man and still remain with her first husband; and the Mormons believe that all her children will belong to the man to whom she is sealed.
Next, I was sealed to my fourteenth wife, Emeline Vaughn. In 1851, I was sealed to my fifteenth wife, Mary Lear Groves. In 1856, I was sealed to my sixteenth wife, Mary Ann Williams.

In temples of God, families are eternally sealed through this power. Couples who enter into the Covenant of Eternal Marriage are sealed together, meaning that their union on earth is also valid in the heavens, rather than ending at death. Children who are subsequently born to them or later sealed to them are theirs for eternity… In addition, temple sealings are performed by proxy for the dead, with spouses sealed to each other and children sealed to parents.

glosses: To form a sacred commitment.

examples.text: What was that office, or work, to which his Father sealed him? I answer, more generally, he was sealed to the whole work of mediation for us, thereby to recover and save all the elect, whom the Father had given him:

Let us all strive to get ourselves sealed to redemption, seeing God doth seal those whom he will deliver in that great day; if we be not in this number, we shall not escape damnation.
Thus these representatives of humanity are first sealed to help with the final work of salvation.

glosses: To fry (meat) at a high temperature to retain the juices.

examples.text: Seal the meat and continue frying until nicely browned.

examples.text: Cette bruine est un personnage, un acteur discret. Elle plombe l’ambiance, aggravant la malédiction qui pèse sur le héros.

examples.text: Partout, en l’air, la voûte énorme et cambrée plombait, si basse que le bras levé d’un homme pouvait l’atteindre.
